If Pages keep borrowing the same fields, stop issuing duplicates like raffle tickets. Put them in a Shared Profile and let inheritance do the legwork.
Author each reusable property once in the canonical Profile. Clones seem efficient until they grow moustaches and disagree.
Adopt a published Saved Schema when lineage matters. It keeps the family tree attached, including the branch everyone insists is not theirs.
Concepts arrange Profile properties into sensible documentation gangs. Validation remains unmoved; it has its own clipboard.
Only defined fields shuts the schema gate to surprise extras. Inherited policy still has a key, because bureaucracy loves hierarchy.
Give each Page its observed page event before polishing the schema. Even a splendid room needs a doorbell before anyone can prove they visited.
Path conditions are the Page's doorman: they inspect each observed location and politely—or firmly—decide whether it belongs.
Order Property Set memberships deliberately. Otherwise their schema contributions arrive like five inspectors all claiming the same chair.
Attach a Shared Profile when a Page needs reusable fields. Copying them by hand only breeds tiny paperwork rebellions later.
Review the effective Page schema before adding a local override. Magnify first, meddle second; the ancestors may already have done the work.
Group Pages that share applicability or schema contributions. It is a club with useful paperwork, not matching blazers.
Property Set conditions decide where the shared contribution applies. Make them observable; crystal balls produce dreadful test evidence.
Keep shared fields canonical at the group level so member Pages inherit one story instead of exchanging contradictory telegrams.
Reorder group contributions only after checking affected Pages and Flow instances. Moving one chair can upset the entire schema orchestra.
When contributions quarrel, open the named Property Set from the evidence. Repair the culprit, not every innocent bystander in the corridor.
Give the Event its exact production name. Aliases are charming at parties and catastrophic when the observer is taking attendance.
Choose the source that truly carries this Event. Listening at the wrong pipe produces silence, confusion, and an unnecessarily stern clipboard.
Set the payload target before wiring Assignments. Otherwise the data arrives heroically with nowhere to put its hat.
Associate interaction Events with the Pages and Flows where they occur. Context keeps the custard pie attached to the correct scene.
Refine Event data through canonical contributors instead of duplicating properties. One trustworthy witness beats a chorus of improvisers.
Order Applicability Sets deliberately; higher matches speak first. Without priority, every candidate lunges for the same megaphone.
Build conditions from observable, type-compatible data. The engine understands evidence, not meaningful eyebrow movements.
Keep one truthful fallback for observations matching nothing specific. Every mystery needs a sensible exit, preferably not through the shrubbery.
Run preflight for overlapping Applicability Sets. Two winners are not twice as correct; they are one argument wearing two hats.
Use Applicability Sets to steer Assignments toward the right contributor. It is traffic control for data, minus the tiny fluorescent jacket.
Pages are the rooms; Events are the custard pies. Add the rooms first, then put each splat where it actually happened.
Use Page frames to show where each journey step occurs. A loose Event on the carpet is evidence, but not the helpful sort.
Place each Event occurrence inside its owning Page frame and state its obligation. Containment keeps the plot from wandering off at intermission.
Connect Page frames to Page frames. Events belong inside them; asking an Event to become a road sign is above its pay grade.
Refresh Documentation after changing a selected Flow. The old value map is loyal, polished, and confidently describing yesterday.
Capture representative observations for the path you mean to test. One heroic sample cannot impersonate the entire visiting public.
Record the expected outcome, not merely the raw sample. Evidence without an expectation is just data loitering near a clipboard.
Link each Fixture to the Page, Event, and Flow it demonstrates. Context tells the detective which room contains the footprint.
Use guided validation to compare a Fixture with the compiled specification. Let the machinery argue with the evidence while you supervise.
Incomplete Fixture coverage is advisory, not a schema blockade. It waves a small warning flag; canonical validation still guards the gate.
Choose the observed Event before mapping its Assignment. Even the finest parcel needs a name on the label.
Select an Applicability Set that yields one clear context. Ambiguity is simply two confident ushers pointing at different seats.
Point the Assignment at the contributor that owns the schema. Data dislikes being delivered to a building marked Probably Here.
Use priority only to settle otherwise valid competing candidates. It is a tie-breaker, not a ceremonial crown for your favourite.
Run preflight before testing. Missing targets and tied candidates are easier to catch before they put on matching moustaches.
Refresh the preview after changing a Documentation Set. Yesterday's snapshot is beautifully formatted and completely unaware of today.
Select only the sections this audience needs. A document containing everything is a cupboard falling open, not a briefing.
Order and include Concepts to keep grouped tables consistent. Otherwise the headings queue like shoppers who have spotted a second till.
Save the project-local theme before refreshing the preview. Unsaved branding is just a splendid waistcoat left on the chair.
Generate rich copy or Excel only after refreshing the preview. Exporting stale work merely gives yesterday better stationery.
